title: Thread the captured compose execution id into the compose report, in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-comp
description:
Thread the captured compose execution id into the compose report, in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts. Two insertions, both purely additive, no existing line deleted or changed. All anchors below were verified verbatim-unique against the current file.

First insertion. The line

  try {

that immediately precedes the verbatim-unique line

    const traceEndpoint = process.env["METABOB_ENDPOINT"] ?? "http://127.0.0.1:8080";

gets one new statement inserted directly ABOVE that `try {` line:

  let emittedExecutionId: string | null = null;

And inside that same try-block, directly after the verbatim-unique line

        console.log(`[feature-compose] trace emission persisted execution_id=${emittedId}`);

insert:

        emittedExecutionId = emittedId;

Second insertion. In the resolver's final return — the object whose body begins with the verbatim-unique line

      ok: effectiveVerdict === "FAVORABLE",

insert one new field directly after that line:

      execution_id: emittedExecutionId,

Both insertions must land together; the value flows from the first to the second, so a draft carrying only one of them does not address this goal.

Why: the trace store already returns the compose run's real exec_* row id when the trace is posted, and the current code reads it into a const named emittedId whose only consumer is the console.log above — the id is captured and then discarded. Because it never reaches the returned featureComposeReport, the caller synthesizes feature_compose:<commit-sha> as the execution id, which matches no row, so no reach verdict can ever address the compose run's actual record: self-development has 5 graded rows in three weeks against 868 ungraded exec_* rows. After this lands, the report body carries an execution_id matching a real row (or null when emission failed, which honestly distinguishes an absent id from a fabricated one), verifiable with one query per compose.
